transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-03-29
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Dr. Anika Rao (Sable Head of Compliance), Luis Moreno (Sable Security), Priya Singh (Sable Legal)

Summary: Quick security and privacy review focused on whether Redwood trains on customer data, data residency options for EU and APAC, KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs and retention, and how Redwood handles PII/PHI. Customer asked for explicit contractual language around 'no training' and an outline of what logs look like for auditors. Redwood agreed to share SOC 2 artifacts, KMS integration docs, and run a small PHI flow test on Private instance.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate the time. Quick roll call - Ethan and I from Redwood, and then...
[00:06] Dr. Anika: Hi, this is Anika, hi.
[00:08] Luis: Luis here.
[00:09] Priya: Priya joining from legal.
[00:11] Maya: Great. Goal for today is to walk through our controls around data handling, address the "no training" ask, and run through KMS/residency options. Ethan will chime in for the technical bits.

[00:30] Ethan: Hi all. Quick TL;DR: hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private, and the guarantees differ. On hosted we have strong isolation and config but customer data may touch our control plane; on Dedicated you get reserved capacity, and Private gives you a customer-controlled VPC and optional on-prem. For strict no-exfiltration/no-training requirements we recommend Private or Dedicated with contractual commitments.

[01:05] Dr. Anika: When you say "no training" can you be explicit — we need confirmation that customer prompts and completions will never be used to train models or to improve model weights. That's a showstopper for us otherwise we need full anonymization.

[01:20] Ethan: Absolutely. Short answer: Redwood's default policy is we do not train customer models on request content. We have a company-wide rule and technical safeguards. For hosted customers we can contractually commit no training and we also have a flag in our ingestion pipeline that tags data as do-not-train. I should caveat that there are aggregated telemetry signals used for platform health but those are anonymized and do not contain customer prompt text.

[01:55] Luis: How is that enforced technically? Could someone flip a flag and accidentally allow training?

[02:05] Ethan: Good question. The flag is set at ingestion and is enforced by the pipeline gating system. It's part of the data flow policy in the control plane. There are RBAC restrictions — only our platform data ops role can change pipeline configs and those actions are logged. We also have automated tests that validate the do-not-train tag propagates. For Private deployments the data never leaves the customer's VPC unless you opt in.

[02:30] Priya: We will want contractual language in the MSA that explicitly states: Redwood will not use customer-provided content to train or improve any model without explicit written consent. Also need definitions: what 'content' includes, does metadata count, telemetry, derived embeddings etc.

[02:55] Maya: That's fair. We can include explicit no-training clauses and define metadata vs content. Our security pack includes a recommended clause, we'll send a redlineable document.

[03:20] [Speaker 2]: Quick note, we also have a separate data retention policy — by default hosted logs are retained 30 days, but we can configure shorter retention and ephemerality for Protected workloads. Dedicated and Private give you retention controls and options to disable retention of prompt text entirely.

[03:47] Dr. Anika: On retention, can you give us the exact scope: are prompts stored, response text, embeddings, logs, request/response headers? We need to know what auditors will see.

[04:00] Ethan: By default logs capture request and response text for debugging for up to 30 days, plus structured metadata (latency, model version). Embeddings and derivatives are treated as customer data; we classify them similarly. For high-compliance customers we offer prompt masking, immediate purge, or we can route to Private where retention of text can be disabled so nothing is written to central logs.

[04:35] Luis: If we use hosted API but need to ensure EU residency for certain PII, how does that work? Do you have EU regions and is the control plane also regionalized?

[04:48] Ethan: We have regionalized compute — EU region endpoints keep inference in region; however, our control plane is logically separated. For EU data residency contractual commitments we use dedicated VPC options or Private deployment residing in your region. Note some telemetry for service health is global and anonymized, but we can provide a data residency addendum.

[05:20] Priya: KMS question: does Redwood manage keys or can we bring our own key (BYOK) and HSM? We need a mechanism where key material never leaves our KMS.

[05:33] Ethan: You can BYOK via our KMS integration. We support external KMS providers and have HSM-backed integrations. For Private deployments you can use customer-managed KMS and we never store plaintext keys. For hosted we offer envelope encryption where your KMS performs the master key wrapping and Redwood holds wrapped keys only.

[06:00] Dr. Anika: Audit logs — auditors will want a log of who accessed what prompt and when. Can you produce immutable audit logs and retention for two years?

[06:12] Maya: Our platform emits audit logs with user identities (SSO/SAML / SCIM integ), resource IDs, and operations. For Hosted and Dedicated we can ship logs to your SIEM via syslog or S3 export. Immutability/retention for two years is doable via export to your log store or managed retention. For Private on-prem we recommend local immutability controls.

[06:45] Luis: SSO — we need SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning, and RBAC with at least roles for admin, dev, auditor. Does Redwood support that out of the box?

[06:58] Ethan: Yes SAML 2.0 and SCIM supported. RBAC roles exist for Admin, Operator, Auditor, Engineer. You can scope token issuance and set granular permissions per-organization and per-project. We also have session timeout policies and MFA requirement support.

[07:20] Priya: HIPAA/PHI — we are a medtech company, a lot of our prompts will include PHI. Do you sign a BAA and what safeguards beyond encryption do you provide?

[07:33] Ethan: Redwood can sign a BAA for Private and Dedicated customers. Technically we provide encryption in transit (TLS1.3), at rest (AES-256), KMS integrations, strict network controls, and data segregation. We also offer optional on-prem package that keeps all processing inside your network for highest assurance. We'll share our BAA template. Note hosted customers can be covered but typically we recommend Dedicated or Private for PHI.

[08:10] Dr. Anika: Is there any chance of data being used to improve model prompts or RLHF? I want to restate this — no RLHF or fine-tuning on our prompts.

[08:20] Ethan: Confirmed: no fine-tuning or RLHF on customer prompt text without explicit opt-in. We use synthetic/regression test corpora and open data for model training pipelines, not customer prompt corpus. There is an internal compliance review before any training dataset accepts new sources.

[08:45] [00:09:00] Maya: I'll pause there. Anything else on training?

[09:02] Luis: How do you handle de-identification? If we want to send PHI to the model but ensure NPI is masked, do you offer built-in PII redaction or client-side tokenization?

[09:18] Ethan: We have two patterns: client-side redaction where you replace identifiers before sending, and server-side transformation hooks in Private where you can run a redaction lambda inside your VPC prior to inference. We also have a managed PII scrubber as an add-on but recommend client-side for maximum control.

[09:45] Priya: For auditors, can you provide a sample of what a request log line looks like? We need field names and sample values.

[09:56] Ethan: Yes — we'll include a sample log schema in the security pack. It will show timestamp, org_id, project_id, user_id, model_id, request_id, latency_ms, and optionally request_text/response_text if retention is enabled. We'll also include the S3 export example for immutability.

[10:20] Dr. Anika: Encryption at rest — is it double wrapped or single? Are backups encrypted?

[10:28] Ethan: We use envelope encryption — data keys are encrypted with a master key stored in customer or Redwood KMS depending on configuration. Backups are encrypted with the same envelope approach and we log key usage. For BYOK, your master never leaves your KMS.

[10:50] Luis: Can you show us where to find SOC 2 and ISO artifacts?

[10:56] Maya: We'll send links. We have SOC 2 Type II report available under NDA; ISO 27001 certificate link is in the pack. We'll attach them to the follow-up email.

[11:12] [Speaker 1]: Customer asked about timeline for a proof-of-concept if we do Dedicated vs Private. Any roughs?

[11:20] Ethan: Dedicated provisioning is usually 2-4 weeks for reserved capacity and network peering; Private on-prem can be longer depending on networking, but our Private cloud appliance has a typical 4-8 week timeline for complex regulated installs. We can do a quick pilot on hosted in days for evaluation with the no-training flag enabled.

[11:50] Priya: If we enable no-training flag on hosted for pilot, will that be auditable? We need proof that data wasn't fed back into training.

[12:02] Ethan: Yes we can provide evidence: ingestion logs showing do-not-train tag, pipeline config snapshots, and the training dataset review logs that show sources used in a given training window. That gives auditors a chain of custody showing your data wasn't in training sets.

[12:28] Luis: What about anomalies — if a dev accidentally toggles retention to on, how do you detect and remediate?

[12:36] Ethan: We have alerting on config drift, role-based change approvals, and an immutable audit trail. In addition, we have guardrails that prevent enabling retention on accounts under certain compliance flags without a multi-actor approval flow.

[12:58] Dr. Anika: For the BAA and MSA language — will Redwood accept a 'no derivatives' clause that also prohibits creating embeddings or other derivatives used for model improvement?

[13:12] Maya: We can discuss precise wording. Embeddings and derivatives are treated as customer data; they won't be used for improvement without consent. We'll propose a clause that explicitly lists embeddings, prompts, responses, and derived features as protected.

[13:30] [13:30] Ethan: Quick tangent — on telemetry for platform safety we collect abstracted usage patterns (e.g., token counts, error rates) but we strip the content. That data is used for routing/batching optimizations only.

[13:50] Luis: Do you have certifications for encryption standards or HSM?

[13:55] Ethan: We partner with cloud KMS providers that are FIPS 140-2/3 compliant and have HSM-backed keys. Our Private deployment uses industry-standard HSM integrations.

[14:15] Priya: A practical question — for the pilot we need to run 1) a PHI redaction flow, 2) export of audit logs to our SIEM, 3) contractual no-training. Can Redwood do these simultaneously?

[14:30] Maya: Yes, that's the plan. For speed we recommend starting on hosted with no-training flag + audit export to S3 with short retention, while we spin up Dedicated or Private for long-term. We'll include a recommended pilot checklist in the follow-up.

[14:55] Dr. Anika: How about cost implications — does disabling retention add cost or reduce costs?

[15:05] Ethan: Disabling retention reduces storage cost but may increase troubleshooting time. Private/Dedicated have fixed costs for reserved capacity; host vs private pricing differ. We'll include a cost impact note in the pilot checklist.

[15:30] Priya: We will need a copy of the pipeline gating audit and the SOP for do-not-train enforcement.

[15:40] Ethan: We'll include an excerpted SOP and architecture diagram showing gating points and control plane checks.

[16:00] Maya: Recap: Redwood to send SOC2/ISO links (under NDA), BAA template and proposed no-training clause, KMS/BYOK integration doc, sample log schema, pilot checklist with estimated timelines and cost notes. Ethan to run a quick PHI flow test in Private and share results. Customer to provide residency priority and legal redlines.

[16:25] Priya: Sounds good. We'll review the BAA and try to get redlines back within two weeks.

[16:30] Dr. Anika: One last question — do you provide a signed attestation that specific org IDs were excluded from training for a given time window?

[16:39] Ethan: Yes, we can provide attestation artifacts: ingestion snapshots, do-not-train tags, and training dataset manifests for the training windows in question. It's part of the compliance deliverables for enterprise customers.

[16:58] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the pack today. Any final questions?

[17:05] Luis: None here. Thank you.
[17:07] Priya: Thanks, bye.

[17:10] Anika: Thanks all, bye.

End of transcript.
